Theorem 3 claims that an MV-permissive STM satisfying UP GC cannot make read-only transactions invisible: a solo read-only transaction must change the configuration external to it. Here, assuming only that fresh read-only transactions on fresh threads exist (`FreshRO`), we exhibit a valid STM (strictly serializable, MV-permissive, reads return written and kept versions, garbage collection is final) that satisfies Definition 4 literally and in which *every* solo read-only transaction leaves the configuration external to it unchanged (`STM.NoTrace`). This refutes both the paper's universal phrasing ("every solo read-only transaction changes the external configuration") and the existential one proved in `theorem_3` (under the potential-reader reading of UP GC). The STM is `snapSmall`, the eager snapshot STM whose read-only transactions erase themselves from the shared memory at commit.
